rules.formula: IC; however, IC. / IC. However, IC.
rules.note: however belongs to the second clause: the second clause contrasts with the first. Strong stop (; or .) BEFORE however, comma AFTER it.

rules.zh: however 結束第一句（與前一句對比）
rules.note: however belongs to the first clause: that clause contrasts with the sentence before it, and the second clause explains or supports it. Ask: which clause is the contrast?

rules.zh: however 插入同一句（成對逗號）
rules.note: Only one independent clause. however just interrupts it, so it takes a pair of commas. A semicolon would cut the subject off from its verb.

rules.formula: IC, though. / IC, though; IC. / Subject, though, verb.
rules.note: As an adverb, though works exactly like however. Its favorite SAT position is the end of a clause: , though; or , though.

rules.formula: Though DC, IC. / IC, though DC.
rules.zh: though = although（連接詞，不可接在分號/句號後）
rules.note: As a conjunction, though starts a dependent clause. Join it to the main clause with a comma (or nothing). Never put ; . : right before it: the though-clause becomes a fragment.

rules.formula: ✗ IC, however, IC. ✗ Although X; however, Y.
rules.zh: 常見錯誤：逗號拼接、重複轉折
rules.note: A comma cannot join two independent clauses, even with however/though in between (comma splice). And although/though already show contrast, so adding however is redundant.

questions.passage: Monarch butterflies travel up to 4,800 kilometers each autumn to reach their wintering grounds in central Mexico. For decades, researchers assumed the insects relied mainly on the sun to find their way. The sun is an unreliable guide on cloudy ______ monarchs still manage to stay on course when skies are overcast. Later studies found that the butterflies can also sense Earth's magnetic field.
questions.marked: [1|The sun is an unreliable guide on cloudy days]⟨;⟩ {however}⟨,⟩ [2|monarchs still manage to stay on course]  [d|when skies are overcast].

why.A: Two independent clauses; however starts the second → ; however,
why.B: , however, between two ICs = comma splice.
why.C: No punctuation between the ICs = run-on.

questions.passage: For much of the twentieth century, scientists believed that adult human brains could not grow new neurons. Brain cells, they thought, were formed only before birth and in early childhood. The idea seemed to match what doctors observed in patients with brain ______ studies in the 1990s found evidence that new neurons can form in the adult hippocampus, a region linked to memory.
questions.marked: [1|The idea seemed to match what doctors observed in patients with brain injuries]⟨.⟩ {However}⟨,⟩ [2|studies in the 1990s found evidence that new neurons can form in the adult hippocampus, a region linked to memory].

why.A: Period ends IC1; However, opens IC2 (the 1990s studies contrast with the old idea).
why.D: Needs a comma after introductory However.

questions.passage: Geoscientists have long considered Hawaii’s Mauna Loa volcano to be Earth’s largest shield volcano by volume, measuring approximately 74,000 cubic kilometers. _______ according to a 2020 study by local geoscientist Michael Garcia, Hawaii’s Pūhāhonu shield volcano is significantly larger, boasting a volume of about 148,000 cubic kilometers.
questions.marked: [1|Geoscientists have long considered Hawaii’s Mauna Loa volcano to be Earth’s largest shield volcano by volume][p|, measuring approximately 74,000 cubic kilometers]⟨.⟩ {However}⟨,⟩ [p|according to a 2020 study by local geoscientist Michael Garcia,] [2|Hawaii’s Pūhāhonu shield volcano is significantly larger][p|, boasting a volume of about 148,000 cubic kilometers].

why.D: The new study contradicts the long-held view → contrast. Punctuation already fixed: . However,
why.B: The study is not a result of the old belief.
why.C: Moreover adds a similar point; this is the opposite.

questions.passage: Sociologist Alton Okinaka sits on the review board tasked with adding new sites to the Hawai‘i Register of Historic Places, which includes Pi‘ilanihale Heiau and the ‘Ōpaeka‘a Road Bridge. Okinaka doesn’t make such decisions _______ all historical designations must be approved by a group of nine other experts from the fields of architecture, archaeology, history, and Hawaiian culture.
questions.marked: [1|Okinaka doesn’t make such decisions single-handedly]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨;⟩ [2|all historical designations must be approved by a group of nine other experts]…

why.A: The contrast is sentence 1 vs IC1 (he sits on the board ↔ but doesn't decide alone). IC2 explains IC1, so however stays with IC1.
why.B: Puts however with IC2, but IC2 agrees with IC1 — no contrast there.
why.D: Run-on; no punctuation between the ICs.

questions.passage: During the English neoclassical period (1660–1789), many writers imitated the epic poetry and satires of ancient Greece and Rome. They were not the first in England to adopt the literary modes of classical _______ some of the most prominent figures of the earlier Renaissance period were also influenced by ancient Greek and Roman literature.
questions.marked: [1|They were not the first in England to adopt the literary modes of classical antiquity]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨;⟩ [2|some of the most prominent figures of the earlier Renaissance period were also influenced by ancient Greek and Roman literature].

why.C: IC1 contrasts with sentence 1 (they imitated ↔ but weren't the first). IC2 supports IC1 (“also”).
why.A: Comma splice (nothing strong between the ICs).
why.D: Links however to IC2, which is not a contrast.

questions.passage: Community gardens have spread rapidly through American cities over the past two decades. Supporters often describe them as a simple way to increase access to fresh produce. The gardens' nutritional impact is difficult to ______ their social effects are easier to document.
questions.marked: [1|The gardens' nutritional impact is difficult to measure]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨;⟩ [2|their social effects are easier to document].

why.D: IC1 pushes back on sentence 2 (“simple way to increase access to fresh produce”), so however closes IC1.
why.B: Missing comma after however (and wrong clause).

questions.passage: Johann Sebastian Bach was admired in his lifetime mainly as an organist rather than as a composer. After his death in 1750, much of his music was rarely performed. The young composer ______ helped change that in 1829 when he conducted a revival of the St. Matthew Passion in Berlin.
questions.marked: [1:Subject|The young composer Felix Mendelssohn]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|helped change that in 1829] [d|when he conducted a revival of the St. Matthew Passion in Berlin].

why.D: One clause; however sits between subject and verb → paired commas.
why.A: Semicolon cuts the subject off from its verb.

questions.passage: Some scientists think that the first Americans walked across a land bridge from Siberia about 13,000 years ago. ______ argue that early migrants traveled by boat along the Pacific coast.
questions.marked: [1:Subject|Others]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|argue] [d:noun clause|that early migrants traveled by boat along the Pacific coast].

why.C: “Others” alone is not a clause; a semicolon can't follow it.

questions.src: Official · Digital SAT 3 – Module 1 Q25 (also SAT 9 M1 Q22)
questions.passage: Journalists have dubbed Gil Scott-Heron the “godfather of rap,” a title that has appeared in hundreds of articles about him since the 1990s. Scott-Heron himself resisted the godfather _______ feeling that it didn’t encapsulate his devotion to the broader African American blues music tradition as well as “bluesologist,” the moniker he preferred.
questions.marked: [1|Scott-Heron himself resisted the godfather nickname]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨,⟩ [p|feeling that it didn’t encapsulate his devotion to the broader African American blues music tradition as well as “bluesologist,” the moniker he preferred].

why.C: What follows is a participial phrase (feeling…), not a clause. Still one sentence → paired commas.
why.B: A semicolon needs an IC after it; “feeling…” is not one.
why.D: Same problem: no IC after the semicolon.

questions.passage: Most people picture the Sahara as an endless sea of sand dunes. Dunes cover only about a quarter of the ______ of the rest consists of rocky plateaus, gravel plains, and mountains.
questions.marked: [1|Dunes cover only about a quarter of the desert]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨.⟩ [2|Much of the rest consists of rocky plateaus, gravel plains, and mountains].

why.A: though (= however) ends IC1 and contrasts with sentence 1; period starts IC2.
why.B: “; though much…” → though becomes a conjunction after a semicolon = fragment.

questions.passage: Chondrites are stony meteorites that are undifferentiated—that is, their contents have not melted and separated into distinct layers. They are hardly _______ many chondrites experience aqueous alteration as a result of exposure to fluids, as well as fracturing, veining, and localized melting due to collisions with other objects.
questions.marked: [1|They are hardly pristine]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨;⟩ [2|many chondrites experience aqueous alteration as a result of exposure to fluids, as well as fracturing, veining, and localized melting]…

why.B: IC1 contrasts with sentence 1 (undifferentiated ↔ hardly pristine); IC2 gives the evidence.
why.C: “; though many…” turns IC2 into a fragment.

questions.passage: Digital artist Jung (Lulu) Chen primarily uses a suite of software tools to create illustrations for children’s books. To manifest the warm and welcoming atmospheres that are a signature of her _______ she occasionally relies on more traditional art techniques, such as painting with watercolors.
questions.marked: [p|To manifest the warm and welcoming atmospheres] [d|that are a signature of her work]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨,⟩ [1|she occasionally relies on more traditional art techniques][p|, such as painting with watercolors].

why.A: Only one IC. though interrupts it (between intro phrase and main clause) → paired commas.
why.C: Semicolon needs ICs on both sides; “To manifest…” is a phrase.

questions.passage: Emily Dickinson wrote nearly 1,800 poems during her lifetime. Fewer than a dozen of them were published while she was alive, and most of those appeared without her name. Though she rarely left her family's home in Amherst, ______ she exchanged letters with dozens of friends, editors, and relatives.
questions.marked: «Though»[d|she rarely left her family's home in Amherst, Massachusetts]⟨,⟩ [1|she exchanged letters with dozens of friends, editors, and relatives].

why.C: Semicolon leaves the though-clause a fragment.
why.D: Period leaves the though-clause a fragment.

questions.passage: Over the centuries, the lean grew so severe that engineers closed the tower to visitors in 1990. A decade of careful work removed soil from beneath the higher ______ though the tower still leans about four degrees today.
questions.marked: [1|A decade of careful work removed soil from beneath the higher side]⟨,⟩ «though»[d|the tower still leans about four degrees today].

why.A: though = although; the DC attaches to the main clause with a comma.
why.C: Colon cannot introduce a DC here.
why.D: “Though the tower still leans…” alone = fragment.

questions.passage: A cheetah can accelerate from 0 to about 95 kilometers per hour in roughly three seconds. Though the cheetah is the fastest land ______ it can maintain its top speed for only about 20 to 30 seconds.
questions.marked: «Though»[d|the cheetah is the fastest land animal]⟨,⟩ [1|it can maintain its top speed for only about 20 to 30 seconds].

questions.passage: In 1900, about a third of the cars in the United States were electric. Electric cars were quiet, clean, and easy to ______ gasoline cars soon came to dominate the market.
questions.marked: [1|Electric cars were quiet, clean, and easy to start]⟨.⟩ {However}⟨,⟩ [2|gasoline cars soon came to dominate the market].
questions.wrong: [1|Electric cars were quiet, clean, and easy to start]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨,⟩ [2|gasoline cars soon came to dominate the market].
questions.wrongLabel: Comma splice: two ICs joined only by commas

why.B: Also a comma splice; though doesn't fix it.

questions.passage: Sloths are famous for moving slowly, and their low metabolism lets them survive on a diet of leaves. Although these animals spend most of their lives hanging in ______ they climb down to the ground about once a week to relieve themselves.
questions.marked: «Although»[d|these animals spend most of their lives hanging in trees]⟨,⟩ [1|they climb down to the ground about once a week to relieve themselves].
questions.wrong: «Although»[d|these animals spend most of their lives hanging in trees]⟨;⟩ {however}⟨,⟩ [1|they climb down to the ground about once a week]…
questions.wrongLabel: Redundant: Although + however both signal contrast; the DC is left as a fragment

why.A: Although already shows the contrast → just a comma.

questions.passage: Koalas live in the eucalyptus forests of eastern Australia. Though it is often called a koala ______ koala is not a bear at all. It is a marsupial, meaning that its young develop in a pouch.
questions.marked: «Though»[d|it is often called a koala bear]⟨,⟩ [1|the koala is not a bear at all].
questions.wrong: «Though»[d|it is often called a koala bear]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨,⟩ [1|the koala is not a bear at all].

why.D: “Though it is often called a koala bear.” = fragment.
